IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-INC-4821 — multiple services reporting elevated 5xx rate and backend latency. Auto-tags: db, cache, pgbouncer, page-oncall
PagerDuty: PagerDuty: routed to eng-oncall (priority: high). Escalation policy: primary -> secondary after 5m.
Sara O: acked. I'm on it, will triage.
James L: I'm grabbing metrics, looks like redis.accept_queue is spiking and pgbouncer wait queue length increasing. also seeing pg replica lag jump.
Nina K: putting DB logs on watch, checking replica status.
Arjun P: any customer-facing impact reported? Emily - Support: Support queue shows a few 502s for /v1/embeddings and increased latency for streaming responses. No billing-impact alerts yet.
Sara O: ok initial hypothesis: upstream fanout + KV cache miss storm is overwhelming Redis clients and exhausting pgbouncer max_client slots, causing app timeouts -> 502s.
James L: metric snippets:
```
redis_total_clients: 10240 -> maxclients (90%)
redis_accept_queue: 1200 -> median 900
pgbouncer_waiting_clients: 250 -> max_wait 02:12
pg_replica_lag_seconds: primary->replica 00:03:45
apiserver_5xx_rate: 4.3% -> spike from 0.2%
```
Sara O: running quick checks: `kubectl get pods -n redwood | grep pgbouncer` shows 3 pgbouncer pods in us-west-2. pgbouncer config max_client_conn currently 2048.
Nina K: looking at pg side: there are a few long-running read queries from report jobs; killing them will reduce replica lag. will coordinate.
Arjun P: can we temporarily increase pgbouncer replicas to relieve wait queue?
James L: autoscaler for pgbouncer is manual; I'll scale horizontally now.
James L: `kubectl scale deploy/pgbouncer -n redwood --replicas=6` -> scaling started.
IncidentBot: deployment/pgbouncer scaled: 3 -> 6 replicas.
Sara O: good. Also pushing a config bump: lower `max_client_conn` per instance is fine since we're adding replicas, keep overall capacity similar but reduce per-pod accept storms. planning to update to 1500.
Arjun P: while scaling completes, Nina, do you want to run `pg_terminate_backend` for the long reports? any risk to data?
Nina K: they're read-only analytic queries, safe to terminate. I'll kill the top 5 longest-running.
Nina K: `SELECT pid, now() - pg_stat_activity.query_start AS runtime, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state='active' AND query NOT ILIKE '%pgbouncer%' ORDER BY runtime DESC LIMIT 5;`
Nina K: terminated 5 sessions, replica lag dropping.
James L: pgbouncer pods are ready. wait queue dropped from 250 -> 30 within 45s. redis accept queue still elevated but client rejects reduced.
Sara O: next: reduce cache miss pressure — enable local prefix caching for embeddings route and increase connection pool for redis clients temporarily in api-workers config. Arjun, can you ship a quick patch?
Arjun P: making a tiny config change, will rollout to production canary (10%).
IncidentBot: canary rollout started for api-workers v2.3.1-canary (10%).
Emily - Support: customers reporting degraded behavior are mostly interactive editors and a few API customers on embeddings. I'm drafting a short status note to affected customers.
PagerDuty: PagerDuty: primary oncall acknowledged. escalation paused.
Sara O: monitoring: 5xx rate down to 1.1%, pgbouncer wait ~25, redis clients steady at 8500. replica lag under 40s and trending down.
James L: logs show earlier connection errors like: `ERROR redis: OOM command rejected` and `FATAL: too many connections` from pgbouncer metrics. those stopped after scaling and terminations.
Sara O: plan for stabilization: keep pgbouncer at 6 for the next 30m, keep canary patch at 10% for 10m then push 100% if no regression, and follow up with a post-incident action to add autoscaling and better throttling on fanout endpoints.
Arjun P: rolling canary -> 100% now. changes applied.
IncidentBot: canary rollout succeeded.
Emily - Support: posted status update to customers in impacted list, noted root cause as transient cache+db connection exhaustion and mitigations applied.
James L: scheduling a short follow-up doc in #eng-postmortems with metric graphs and suggested runbook updates.
Sara O: thanks all. leaving notes: possible follow-ups — add redis client backpressure, global request limiter on embeddings endpoint, pgbouncer horizontal autoscaler, nicer fallbacks for cache miss storms.
Arjun P: i'll open an RFC for adaptive throttling on fanout.
Nina K: adding DB playbook step to detect long analytic queries during peak traffic and circuit-break them.
Sara O: closing pager: PagerDuty acknowledged incident resolved. I'll keep watch for 30m then handback to normal rotation. :white_check_mark:
PagerDuty: PagerDuty: incident resolved by primary oncall.
IncidentBot: auto-note: incident closed by Sara O.
Sara O: leaving final note: no data loss, partial customer impact (temporary 502s for some endpoints), total duration ~26 minutes. postmortem owner: Arjun P.
Emily - Support: I'll follow up with customers who opened tickets. :email:
